title: Registered instruction word + exact one-ahead fetch (take IMEM DO off every R-stage path)

# Registered instruction word + exact one-ahead fetch (take IMEM DO off every R-stage path)

Category: timing

## Motivation

The critical path (5.721 ns → est. 104 MHz) is:

    IMEM RAMB18 CLK->DO           2.55 ns   (no output register: ~2.45 ns clk-to-out)
    row word select (isel, LUT6)  3.02
    ra field -> R-file mux + r0   3.43 / 3.56 / 3.79 (LUT5, LUT5, LUT6)
    w1 = iw[1] + R[ra]            4.05 .. 5.59 (LUT2 x2 + 8 x CARRY4)
    mux -> p_cmd.w1[29]           5.72

That is `dcmd[221]` = `cmd.w1` bit 29. Almost half of the path (2.55 of 5.72 ns) is BRAM
clock-to-out, and every R-stage computation starts from that BRAM output:
- the three register-relative adds (`dcmd.w1/w2/w3`),
- `ADDI` (`R[rd] <= R[ra] + iw[1]`),
- `LOOP` (`lp_cnt <= R[ra] + iw[2]`),
- `icount += r_ret`,
- the fetch loop `op -> pc_n -> IMEM address` (the path the prompt flags as the Vivado risk).

These paths all start 2.1 ns behind a flip-flop-sourced path, so I expect them to account for the
top histogram buckets ((5189, 5727] ns). To reach 110 MHz (logic ≤ 5.37 ns under
`1000/(1.6*t+0.5)`), or +3 % (≤ 5.52 ns), all of these paths have to lose the BRAM delay. Moving
the adds one at a time can't do that: the add in `ADDI` must stay in the fetch cycle.

## Change (rtl/seq/otpu_seq.sv only)

Keep **one BRAM read per cycle**, but put a register between it and the decoder. Aim the BRAM one
instruction ahead, at an exact (not speculative) successor address that is computed from
flip-flops only.

### New state
- `ir` (256 bits): the instruction at `pc`, i.e. the selected 8 words. `iw[k] = ir[32k +: 32]`.
  `op/ra/rb/rc/rd/flags/dcmd/dunit` and the whole R-stage `case` read `ir` instead of `irow`.
- `ir_v`: `ir` holds a valid instruction. It is cleared by `rst`. It is 0 only in the first cycle
  after reset.
- `fa` (32 bits): the pc whose row the BRAM output currently holds. It always equals the pc that
  R moves to next.
- `irow`/`isel` are no longer needed as registers. The BRAM output is `irow <= imem[fa_d / IPR]`,
  with no fabric flip-flops.

### Per cycle
- `ld` means R moves on to the instruction at `fa`:
  `ld = !ir_v || (ir_v && !stopping && !halted && adv)`.
  `adv` is exactly today's "pc_n = next_pc" condition:
  - `op ∈ {NOP, LI, ADDI}`, or
  - `op == LOOP && lp`, or
  - the default branch with `dunit >= 0 && r_take`.
- When `ld`:
  - `pc <= fa`
  - `ir <= irow[256*(fa % IPR) +: 256]` (one 4:1 LUT6 level between DO and a flip-flop, about
    3.1 ns)
  - `ir_v <= 1`
- Holding (LOOP's first cycle, dispatch stall, HALT/stopping/halted, error): `pc`, `ir` and `fa`
  hold, and the BRAM re-reads row `fa`.
- `fa_d` (the next `fa` and the IMEM read address):
  - `rst`: 0.
  - LOOP first cycle (`ir_v && op==LOOP && !lp && !stopping && !halted`):
    `fa_d = (R[ra]+iw[2] == 0) ? pc + 1 + iw[1] : pc + 1`. This is today's second-cycle pc
    choice, made one cycle early, so the LOOP enter/skip costs no bubble.
    - The zero test on the sum is carry-free: `a+b==0 ⇔ ∀i: a_i^b_i == (i==0 ? 0 : a_{i-1}|b_{i-1})`.
    - The value latched into `lp_cnt` is unchanged.
  - `ld`: `fa_d = succ(fa)` under the loop stack as it will be after this edge (below).
  - Otherwise: `fa_d = fa`.
- `succ(x) = (tos valid && tos.end == x && tos.rem > 1) ? tos.start : x + 1`. This is today's
  `next_pc` formula applied to the next instruction. Only the stack top matters, as today.
  "tos after this edge" has four cases, decided by the current instruction's decode. The
  comparisons use flip-flops only and run in parallel with the decode:
  - **A. LOOP 2nd cycle with `lp_cnt != 0` (push).** Here `fa == pc+1`, so the hit condition is
    `lp_len == 1 && lp_cnt > 1`, and the start is `fa`.
  - **B. `advance()` at a loop end with `rem > 1` (decrement).** The hit condition is
    `stk_end[sp-1] == fa && stk_rem[sp-1] > 2`, and the start is `stk_start[sp-1]`.
  - **C. `advance()` at a loop end with `rem <= 1` (pop).** The hit condition is
    `sp >= 2 && stk_end[sp-2] == fa && stk_rem[sp-2] > 1`, and the start is `stk_start[sp-2]`.
  - **D. Otherwise (no stack change, including the post-reset load and a skipped LOOP).** The hit
    condition is `sp != 0 && stk_end[sp-1] == fa && stk_rem[sp-1] > 1`.
  - Only two 32-bit equality comparators are needed (`stk_end[sp-1]==fa`, `stk_end[sp-2]==fa`),
    plus `fa+1`.
- Remove the old `pc_n` / `next_pc` / skip-target logic. `at_end` stays, because `advance()`
  still uses it.
- Gate `r_ret`, the R-stage `case` and `icount`'s `r_ret` with `ir_v`. The case is not entered
  when `!ir_v`.

### Why results are bit-identical

The order in which instructions reach R is unchanged:
- `fa` is by construction the value the old `pc_n` would have taken when R advances. It uses the
  same `next_pc` rule, the same stack contents (the stack only changes when R advances, and those
  changes are folded in through cases A–D), and the same LOOP target.
- Holds don't touch the stack, so `fa` stays valid across them.
- Register reads, the adds, dispatch order, the scoreboard and unit starts are untouched. They
  just see the same instruction stream, sourced from `ir`.
- Loader writes happen only in reset. The first row read after reset (row 0 at the last reset
  edge) is the same read as today.
- The only timing difference is **+1 cycle at program start** (the `!ir_v` load cycle). There is
  no bubble on LOOP enter or skip, and none on loop back-edges. The perf proxy should move by a
  handful of cycles out of many thousands, well under 0.2 %.

## Expected
- **Flip-flops:** +256 (`ir`) + 33 (`fa`, `ir_v`) ≈ +290 FF, from 10944 to about 11235.
- **LUTs:**
  - Added: the 256 word-select LUTs move from after DO to before `ir` (same count), plus about
    +22 for the 2 equality comparators, about +32 for `fa+1`, about +40 for the address muxes and
    about +40 for the carry-free zero test.
  - Removed: the old `pc_n`/`next_pc`/skip mux (about −64).
  - Net about +70–120 LUT.
- **Area-equivalent:** about +215–265 (+0.7–0.9 %), under the +1 % cap for the fmax route.
- **Timing:**
  - All BRAM-sourced paths end at `ir` at about 3.1 ns.
  - The dispatch adds become `ir`(0.3) + R-mux (~1.0) + 32-bit add (~1.6) + mux ≈ 3.2–3.5 ns.
  - The fetch-address path becomes flip-flops → decode/compare → mux ≈ 3.0–3.5 ns.
  - The critical path moves to the scoreboard/start logic. It was below the BRAM-sourced paths
    before, so I estimate ≤ 5.2 ns, giving **est. fmax about 112–118 MHz (+8–13 %)**.
- **Vivado:** the fetch loop (DO → isel → decode → pc_n → ADDR) is gone. DO now feeds one LUT and
  then a flip-flop.

## Risks
- **Loop-stack corner cases in `succ`:**
  - one-instruction bodies (A, and B with `end == start`),
  - pop into an outer loop that ends at the next instruction (C),
  - a LOOP sitting at an enclosing loop's end (LOOP never calls `advance()`, so it is case A or D
    and `fa_d` is forced to pc+1 or the skip target in its first cycle, which matches today).

  A mistake here is a wrong fetch, and the bit-exact tests would catch it. I suggest an
  `ifndef SYNTHESIS` assertion `ld && ir_v -> fa == <old pc_n formula>` while developing.
- **Stack overflow (`sp == 4` then push):** the out-of-range index behaves the same as today (not
  valid ISA).
- **Area:** if the net LUT count comes in higher than estimated, area could brush +1 %. If it
  does, make `lp_len` store `pc+iw[1]` (the end) plus a 1-bit `iw[1]==1` flag. That removes a
  32-bit add and compare from cycle 2.
- **Trace output:** trace lines (`$display`) shift by one cycle. Only timing changes; the
  protocols (`ustart`/`urdy`/`udone`/`urel`, `halted`, `icount` at halt) are unchanged.

# Registered instruction word + exact one-ahead fetch (rtl/seq/otpu_seq.sv)

- New `ir` (256b, the instruction at `pc`), `ir_v` and `fa` (the pc that R moves to next). The IMEM
  block RAM reads `imem[fa_d / IPR]` (it has no fabric flip-flops). `ir <= irow[256*(fa%IPR) +: 256]` when `ld`, so every R-stage
  path (decode, the `w1..w3` adds, ADDI, LOOP, `icount`) now starts at a flip-flop. `irow`/`isel`,
  `pc_n` and `next_pc` are gone. `pc <= fa` on `ld`. `at_end`/`advance()` are unchanged.
- `ld = !ir_v || (!stopping && !halted && adv)`, where `adv` is the old `pc_n = next_pc` condition.
  `fa_d` is 0 in reset. In a LOOP's first cycle it is the enter/skip target, using a carry-free
  zero test `(a^b) == ((a|b)<<1)` on `R[ra]+iw[2]`. On `ld` it is `succ(fa)` under the post-edge stack
  (cases A/B/C/D from HYPOTHESIS, 2 equality comparators). Otherwise it holds.
- The R-stage `case` and `r_ret` are gated by `ir_v`. The only timing difference is +1 cycle at program start.
- I added an `ifndef SYNTHESIS` `$fatal` check: on every `ld && ir_v`, `fa` must equal the old
  `pc_n` formula (`next_pc`, or the LOOP enter/skip target).
- Verification: lint is clean; `test_mlp_rtl[1]` and `test_fuzz_single_slice`/`test_fuzz_two_slices` pass. I also ran a
  scratch nested-loop fuzzer outside the repo (160 programs: 1-instruction bodies, 4-deep nesting,
  pops into an outer loop ending at the next instruction, zero-trip counts from register wrap). All
  160 are bit-identical to isasim. Deliberately breaking case A or case C trips the `$fatal` at once.
lesson: otpu_seq: registering the IMEM word (256b ir) with an exact one-ahead fetch raised fmax 10.5% but cost 1.7% area. Next try: trim the ir width or put the register on the BRAM output (DOB_REG) to stay within +1% area.

title: Cheaper scoreboard comparators (3-bit digit compare) + register adds moved off the IMEM path
hypothesis:
# Cheaper scoreboard comparators (3-bit digit compare) + register adds moved off the IMEM path

Category: area (primary), with a timing part that the acceptance rule requires

## Motivation

**Area.** Almost all LUTs go to the scoreboard. `conflict()` is evaluated for the C-stage
footprint `c_fp` against every one of the WIN = 16 slots. Each call does 20 `ov()` tests
(n.wr x e.rd = 8, e.wr x n.rd = 8, n.wr x e.wr = 4). Each test has two 32-bit unsigned
`<` compares, which gives 40 comparators per slot and **640 32-bit comparators** in total.
`conflict_dram()` reuses the same `lo`/`hi` compares, so opt_merge shares them.
synth_xilinx turns each `$lt` into a `$alu` with one LUT2 per bit
(S = A XNOR B, DI = A) plus 8 CARRY4. That is about 640 x 32 = 20.5k LUTs out of 21 010.
The rest of the design (window storage, R file, fetch muxes) is in FFs and LUT-RAM.
The comparators are therefore the one place where a real area saving exists.

**Timing.** An area-only change is rejected at the current 104 MHz because the rule also needs
est fmax >= 110 MHz. That means the logic delay must fall from 5.721 ns to about 5.4 ns or
less; about 5.0 ns would be safe. The critical path is IMEM DO (2.55 ns, no output register)
-> isel word mux -> `ra` -> R-file 16:1 mux / `rv()` zero test -> **32-bit adder
(carry4 x8, 4.048 -> 5.594 ns)** -> `dcmd.w1[29]` -> `p_cmd`.
The same "IMEM -> R[ra] -> 32-bit add -> FF" structure exists three times:
- the dispatch adds `w1/w2/w3 += R[ra/rb/rc]`
- the ADDI write `R[rd] <= R[ra] + w1`
- the LOOP count `lp_cnt <= R[ra] + w2`

All three have to leave the IMEM cycle.

## Change (only rtl/seq/otpu_seq.sv)

### Part A: comparators built from 3-bit digits (area)

Add local functions in otpu_seq. Do not use the package's `conflict`/`conflict_dram` in the
module, and leave otpu_pkg unchanged.

```systemverilog
// x < z (unsigned 32-bit) as the carry out of an 11-bit add over 3-bit digits:
// per digit g, eq_g propagates, lt_g generates (le_g = lt_g | eq_g).
// One LUT6 for S = eq_g and one for DI = le_g per 3 bits: 22 LUTs + 3 CARRY4,
// instead of 32 LUTs + 8 CARRY4.
function automatic logic lt32(input logic [31:0] x, input logic [31:0] z);
  logic [32:0] xe, ze; logic [10:0] lt, le; logic [11:0] s;
  xe = {1'b0, x}; ze = {1'b0, z};
  for (int g = 0; g < 11; g++) begin
    // explicit gates, not '<', so Yosys does not build 11 tiny carry chains
    lt[g] = (~xe[3*g+2] & ze[3*g+2]) |
            (~(xe[3*g+2] ^ ze[3*g+2]) & ((~xe[3*g+1] & ze[3*g+1]) |
            (~(xe[3*g+1] ^ ze[3*g+1]) & (~xe[3*g] & ze[3*g]))));
    le[g] = lt[g] | (xe[3*g +: 3] == ze[3*g +: 3]);
  end
  s = {1'b0, le} + {1'b0, lt};
  return s[11];
endfunction
```

`ov_s(a, b)` is `a.v & b.v & (a.sp == b.sp) & lt32(a.lo, b.hi) & lt32(b.lo, a.hi)`.
A single function `conf2(n, e)` returns `{conflict, conflict_dram}`. It computes each of the
20 pair tests once:
- `conflict` is `n.all | e.all | OR(pair)`.
- `conflict_dram` is `n.all | e.all | OR(pair & a.sp == SP_DRAM)`. When `a.sp == b.sp`, this
  is exactly what the package's v-masking does.

`ndep`/`ndepd` use `conf2(c_fp, sfp[i])`.

**Why it is bit-exact.** Take X = le, Y = lt, carry-in 0. The carry into digit g+1 is
`(X_g ^ Y_g) ? c_g : X_g`, which is `eq_g ? c_g : lt_g`, because le_g equals lt_g whenever
eq_g is 0. That is the lexicographic compare from the most significant digit down: the result
is lt at the highest differing digit, and 0 if all digits are equal. So `lt32(x, z) == (x < z)`
for every input, and `ndep`/`ndepd` are the same function as before.

### Part B: register adds moved one stage later, with forwarding (timing)

Every R-file read stays in the R stage, so there are no new read hazards. Only the adds move.

- **LI/ADDI** no longer write R at R. They load a pending write: `pw_v <= (rd != 0)`,
  `pw_rd <= rd`, `pw_a <= (op == OP_LI) ? 0 : rv(ra)`, `pw_b <= iw[1]`. `pw_v` defaults to 0
  in every other cycle. In the next cycle, `if (pw_v) R[pw_rd] <= pw_a + pw_b` runs in every
  non-reset cycle, so it also happens while stopping or halted.
- **Forwarding.** `rv(r)` becomes
  `r == 0 ? 0 : (pw_v && pw_rd == r) ? pw_a + pw_b : R[r]`.
  The sum comes from FFs and is ready early. The only addition on the IMEM path is the
  `ra == pw_rd` compare and one mux level, which replaces the 32-bit carry chain.
  Back-to-back ADDI r1,r1,k still runs at one per cycle and gets the same values: each read
  sees the value that sequential execution would give.
- **LOOP.** The first cycle registers `lp_a <= rv(ra)`, `lp_b <= iw[2]`, `lp_len <= iw[1]`.
  `lp_cnt` becomes a wire `lp_a + lp_b` used in the second cycle, in both `pc_n` (`== 0`) and
  `stk_rem`. That path starts at FFs (add, zero test, pc_n mux), so it is well under the
  IMEM path.
- **Dispatch.** Add one stage O between R and P:
  - O holds `o_v`, `o_cmd` (raw: op, flags, iw[1..7]), `o_x1/o_x2/o_x3 = rv(ra/rb/rc)`,
    `o_unit`, `o_pc`.
  - `o_adv = !p_v || p_adv` and `r_take = !o_v || o_adv`.
  - When `o_adv`: `p_v <= o_v`, and `p_cmd <= o_cmd` with `w1 += o_x1`, `w2 += o_x2`,
    `w3 += o_x3`. This replaces the old `if (r_take) p_v <= 0`; now `if (r_take) o_v <= 0`,
    and R sets `o_v`.
  - `pipe_empty` also requires `!o_v`.
  - P, S, Q and C are unchanged, and P still sees the finished `p_cmd`. The adder is not put
    in front of fp_ops or the DSPs, which are already about 4+ ns.

The commands, their order, the footprints, the dependencies and `icount` are all unchanged.
The only difference is one more cycle of front-end latency, which matters only when the
window runs dry waiting on the front end.

## Expected

- **LUT:** Part A saves about 10 of 32 LUTs per comparator, roughly -4k to -6.4k LUTs
  (up to -30% of LUTs). Part B adds about +0.2k LUTs (forwarding muxes, pw adder). Net
  **about -4k to -6k LUTs**.
- **FF:** about +0.45k. The O stage adds 240 + 96 bits, plus pw (69) and lp_a/lp_b
  (lp_cnt goes away).
- **Area-eq:** 29 930 -> about 24.0k to 26.0k (-13% to -20%).
- **Timing:** removing the carry chain after the IMEM mux takes about 1.6 ns off the worst
  path. IMEM -> operand FFs lands around 4.2 ns. The next limits are likely the fetch loop
  (IMEM -> op decode -> pc_n -> BRAM address, about 4.4 to 4.8 ns) and start selection.
  Est fmax about 115 to 125 MHz, which is >= 110. The scoreboard compare path also gets
  shorter: 3 CARRY4 instead of 8.
- **Perf proxy:** +1 cycle only at front-end refill events. This should be far below the 0.2%
  limit when MM/DMA work dominates.

## Risks

- **ABC mapping.** ABC might not fold `S = le ^ lt` into a single 6-input LUT and could keep
  a separate `lt` LUT, giving 33 LUTs per compare. If the LUT count does not fall, try 2-bit
  digits (S and DI as LUT4s) or check with the `stat` of a small test module.
- **Yosys `<` inference.** Yosys could turn the 3-bit `==` or `<` pieces back into `$alu`.
  That is why the digit logic is written as explicit gates.
- **Forwarding and pending writes.** A bug in forwarding, for example R written twice, or LI
  at R while an older ADDI is pending on the same rd, would change addresses and therefore
  results. The rule is that the older pending write lands at the end of the cycle; the younger
  one becomes pending and wins on reads through `pw_rd`.
- **Front-end latency.** The +1 cycle could cost perf if the proxy has many short,
  front-end-bound phases. It stays well under 0.2% unless the proxy has one refill every
  ~500 cycles.
- **Remaining timing risk.** If the fetch loop (pc_n -> BRAM address) is already at about
  5.4 ns, fmax gains less. In that case Part A still holds the area gain, but acceptance
  needs est fmax >= 110.

title: Split the register-relative adds: low 16 bits at R, high 16 bits one cycle later
hypothesis:
# Split the register-relative adds: low 16 bits at R, high 16 bits one cycle later

Category: timing

## Motivation

The critical path (5.721 ns, est. 103.6 MHz) is
`IMEM DOB (2.550) -> isel word mux (3.022) -> R[ra] read mux + r==0 (LUT5/LUT5/LUT6, 3.794)
-> adder LUTs (4.048) -> 8 x CARRY4 (5.594) -> dcmd.w1[29] -> p_cmd`.
That is `dcmd.w1 = iw[1] + rv(ra)`. The carry chain alone takes 1.67 ns. Two other paths
have the same shape and length:

* `dcmd.w2 = iw[2] + rv(rb)` and `dcmd.w3 = iw[3] + rv(rc)`, both into `p_cmd`;
* ADDI/LI, `R[rd] <= rv(ra) + iw[1]`, into the register file;
* LOOP's first cycle, `lp_cnt <= rv(ra) + iw[2]`.

The histogram points to one family of paths. The top bins (5.19–5.73 ns) have a few dozen
endpoints each and step down evenly by about 0.27 ns per bin. That spacing matches the
CARRY4 ripple: each group of about 4 sum bits lands about 0.11 ns later than the group
below it. These endpoints are the upper bits of these 32-bit adds. Bit 15 of the same adds
arrives at about 5.14 ns (CARRY4 slice 3 CI->O) plus the final LUT, about 5.27 ns.

For +3% fmax we need logic <= 5.546 ns. For the 110 MHz target we need <= 5.37 ns.
Registering the BRAM output was tried in r20260924-001624-s0. It gave +10.5% but cost +1.7%
area because Yosys never uses DO_REG, so the 256-bit `ir` became fabric FFs. This change
leaves the fetch path alone and takes the upper 16 carry bits out of the BRAM cycle,
for about +120 FFs.

## Change (rtl/seq/otpu_seq.sv only)

Identity used: `(a + b) mod 2^32 = { a[31:16] + b[31:16] + c16 , (a[15:0] + b[15:0]) mod 2^16 }`,
where `c16` is the carry out of the low half. This is exact modular arithmetic, so every
resolved value is bit-identical.

1. **Split the register file** into two halves: `logic [15:0] Rl[16]` (bits 15:0) and
   `logic [15:0] Rh[16]` (bits 31:16). Both reset to 0, as `R` does now.
   * `Rl` is written in the R cycle, as today.
   * `Rh` is written one cycle later from a single pending-write register:
     `wb_v, wb_rd[3:0], wb_a[15:0], wb_b[15:0], wb_c`, with
     `wire [15:0] wb_hi = wb_a + wb_b + 16'(wb_c);`
   * The read functions are:
     * `rv_lo(r) = (r==0) ? 0 : Rl[r]`, with no bypass because `Rl` is always current.
     * `rv_hi(r) = (r==0) ? 0 : (wb_v && wb_rd==r) ? wb_hi : Rh[r]`, which bypasses the
       pending write.
   * `rv_hi` only feeds registers: `p_ah`, `wb_a` and `lp_a`. Its extra mux level ends
     around 4.1 ns and is off the critical path.
   * At the top of the non-reset branch: `wb_v <= 0; if (wb_v) Rh[wb_rd] <= wb_hi;`. This
     runs whatever the instruction is, so a pending write before a HALT, or while
     `stopping` is set, still lands. In the reset branch: `wb_v <= 0`.
2. **LI and ADDI**, only when `rd != 0`, as today:
   * ADDI: `Rl[rd] <= lo1[15:0]; wb_v<=1; wb_rd<=rd; wb_a<=rv_hi(ra); wb_b<=iw[1][31:16]; wb_c<=lo1[16];`
   * LI: `Rl[rd] <= iw[1][15:0]; wb_v<=1; wb_rd<=rd; wb_a<=0; wb_b<=iw[1][31:16]; wb_c<=0;`
   * LI also goes through `wb`, so there is only ever one pending high-half write. It can
     never race with an older write to the same register.
   * Back-to-back `ADDI r1,r1,k` works: the low half reads the updated `Rl`, the high half
     takes the bypass, and the newer write lands one cycle after the older one.
3. **Dispatch operands**:
   * Compute `lo1 = {1'b0,iw[1][15:0]} + {1'b0,rv_lo(ra)}`, and `lo2` and `lo3` the same way
     from `rb` and `rc`. These are 17-bit adds; ADDI reuses `lo1`.
   * `dcmd.wk = {iw[k][31:16], lok[15:0]}` for k = 1..3, so the high half stays raw.
   * Next to `p_cmd`, register `p_ah[3] <= {rv_hi(ra), rv_hi(rb), rv_hi(rc)}` and
     `p_cy <= {lo1[16], lo2[16], lo3[16]}`, with the same enable as `p_cmd`.
   * In P, build `p_res = p_cmd` with `p_res.wk[31:16] = p_cmd.wk[31:16] + p_ah[k] + p_cy[k]`.
     Use `p_res` in place of `p_cmd` for both `s_cmd <= p_res` and
     `s_pp <= fp_part(fp_ops(p_res, D, S))`.
   * From S onwards everything, including `scmd`, `ucmd` and the footprints, sees exactly
     the resolved command it sees today, on the same cycle.
   * Why this is safe in P: `fp_ops` only reads `w2[7:0]` (QACT rows), `w3[15:0]` (GATHER
     rows) and `w3` (QACT `o.w[0]`). Only QACT's `w3[31:16]` goes through the new P-stage
     adder: flop, then a 16-bit add (~1.6 ns), then the `o.w` mux, then DSP B for the `ph`
     product. That is about 4.8 ns, below the new 5.27 ns worst.
4. **LOOP**:
   * First cycle: `lp_a <= {rv_hi(ra), rv_lo(ra)}; lp_b <= iw[2];` with no add.
   * Second cycle: use `wire [31:0] lp_cnt = lp_a + lp_b;` in `pc_n` and `stk_rem`. This
     path starts at a flop: add, then ==0, then the pc_n mux, then the IMEM address,
     about 4.6 ns.
   * LOOP already holds pc for a cycle between the two steps, so no cycle is added.

Nothing else changes:
* No pipeline stage or latency is added. R, P, S, Q and C advance on exactly the same
  cycles, so `icount`, dispatch, start, release and HALT timing are cycle-identical. The
  perf proxy is unchanged, not just within 0.2%.
* The register file seen through `rv()` holds the same value in every cycle.
* The unit ports (`ucmd`, `ustart`, `urel`) and the IMEM loader port are untouched.

## Expected

* **Timing:**
  * The dispatch and LI/ADDI paths now end at bit 15 or carry 16 of a 16-bit chain,
    about 5.14–5.27 ns instead of 5.72.
  * Estimated logic time is about 5.3 ns, bounded by any path outside this family. The
    old second bin tops out at 5.458 ns.
  * fmax is about 108 MHz (+4.5%) if one unrelated path sits in the old second bin, and
    about 112 MHz (+8%, above the 110 target) if the top bins are all this adder family,
    which the even stepping suggests.
* **FF:** about +120.
  * Added: `p_ah` 48, `p_cy` 3, `wb` 38, `lp_b` 32.
  * `lp_cnt` becomes the combinational sum, and `lp_a` takes its 32 flops.
  * `R` keeps its 512 bits, split into two halves.
* **LUT:** about +70.
  * Added: the 3x16 bypass muxes (they may fold into the last level of the `Rh` read mux),
    3 small compares, and the 16-bit `wb_hi` adder.
  * The dispatch and LOOP adders move rather than duplicate. The P-stage high halves are
    the same 48 LUT+carry bits that are in R today.
* **Area-equivalent:** about +130, i.e. +0.4%, within the +1% the fmax criterion allows.

## Risks

* **Pending-write edge cases:**
  * An ADDI or LI followed at once by a reader of the same register must take the bypass.
  * ADDI writing the register it reads is handled the same way.
  * A pending write before HALT, reset or `stopping` must still land (or be dropped on
    reset, where R is cleared anyway). Getting the priority of `wb_v <= 0` against the
    ADDI/LI assignment wrong breaks bit-exactness. The later assignment in the
    always_ff must win.
* **Yosys packing:**
  * Yosys may not merge the three `rv_lo`/`rv_hi` reads per port the way I expect.
  * If the `ph[0]` DSP is not absorbed with PREG, the QACT `w3[31:16]` path runs
    add, mux, then DSP B->P comb (2.69 ns) into `s_pp`, about 4.9 ns. That is still
    below 5.27 but is the one new path to check in `sta`.
* **Paths outside this family:** if an unrelated path sits between 5.3 and 5.46 ns, the
  gain is +4.5% rather than +8%. That still clears the +3% gate.
* **Vivado fetch loop:** this change does not touch the fetch loop (BRAM DO -> isel ->
  op decode -> pc_n -> IMEM address). It remains the Vivado-side risk, and a prefetch or
  row buffer can still be layered on top later.

# Split register-relative adds (rtl/seq/otpu_seq.sv only)

- `R[16]` is now `Rl[16]` (bits 15:0, written in the R cycle) and `Rh[16]` (bits 31:16). `Rh` is written one cycle later from a single pending write `wb_{v,rd,a,b,c}`, with `wb_hi = wb_a + wb_b + wb_c`. `rv_lo(r)` has no bypass. `rv_hi(r)` bypasses the pending write when `wb_rd == r`.
- The pending write lands at the top of the non-reset branch before the R-stage case, so it lands even on HALT, `stopping` or `halted`. LI and ADDI (rd != 0) then queue the next write, and because they come later in the always_ff they take priority over `wb_v <= 0`. On reset, `wb_v` is cleared and both halves are zeroed.
- Dispatch: `lo1/lo2/lo3` are 17-bit low-half adds, and `dcmd.w1..w3 = {iw[k][31:16], lok[15:0]}`. `p_ah[3]` and `p_cy[3]` are registered with the same enable as `p_cmd`. In P, a combinational `p_res` finishes the high halves, and it feeds both `s_cmd` and `fp_ops`, so S and later stages see the same resolved command on the same cycle as before.
- ADDI reuses `lo1`. LI queues `wb_a=0, wb_c=0`, so there is only ever one pending high-half write.
- LOOP: the first cycle registers `lp_a = {rv_hi, rv_lo}(ra)` and `lp_b = iw[2]`, and `lp_cnt` is now the wire `lp_a + lp_b`, used in `pc_n` and `stk_rem` in the second cycle.
- No stage or cycle was added, and the ports are unchanged.
- Checked: Verilator lint is clean over RTL_SOURCES plus `otpu_axi_mem.sv`. These tests pass: `test_mlp_rtl[1]`, `test_fuzz_single_slice[0,3]`, `test_fuzz_two_slices[0]`, `test_scoreboard_stress_single_slice[0]`.
- Not checked: the existing tests use small register values, so they probably never carry across bit 16. A directed test with LI of negative values, back-to-back ADDI carrying or borrowing across bit 16, and a LOOP count built from a register high half would close that gap. I could not run such a scratch script in this sandbox.
lesson: Splitting the 32-bit reg-relative adds (low 16 at R, high 16+carry a cycle later via a bypassed pending-write reg) moved the CARRY4 upper bits off the BRAM path: +3.9% fmax, only +0.8% area.

title: Scoreboard with 5 footprint ranges (MM ASCALE shares rd[1]) + registered instruction word
hypothesis:
# Scoreboard with 5 footprint ranges (MM ASCALE shares rd[1]) + registered instruction word

Category: area (primary). It includes the timing fix that the acceptance rule needs, because an area-only change must also reach est fmax >= 110 MHz.

## Motivation

**Where the LUTs are.** The champion's `stat` shows:
- 21 010 LUT, of which 10 540 are LUT6 and 5 974 are LUT5.
- 2 303 CARRY4 and 10 944 FDRE.

The scoreboard compares the C-stage footprint `c_fp` against all WIN = 16 slots. `conflict()` has 20 range pairs per slot:
- n.wr x e.rd: 2x4
- e.wr x n.rd: 2x4
- n.wr x e.wr: 2x2

Each pair has two 32-bit `<` compares, which gives **640 comparators**. `conflict_dram` reuses the same compares.

In this flow Yosys already maps `$lt` through `cmp2lcu`: 3-bit chunks, a P LUT6 and a G LUT6 per chunk, and a 3-CARRY4 lookahead chain. The yosys.log of the champion shows `_80_lcu_cmp_` templates for the `$lt` cells. Each compare therefore costs about 22 LUT + 3 CARRY4:
- 640 x 3 = 1 920 of the 2 303 CARRY4.
- About 14 k of the 21 k LUTs.

The window also stores `sfp[16]`, 16 x 403 bits, as flip-flops. That is about 6.4 k of the 10.9 k FF.

This means that last round's "3-bit digit comparator" idea (r…1624-s1) would have saved nothing: that structure is already what Yosys builds. The only real area lever in the scoreboard is **fewer range pairs**.

**The removable range.** `fp_ranges` fills MM's `rd[1]` with the streamed-scale DRAM range only when `!flags[0]` (UNIT clear). It fills `rd[3]`, the ASCALE TMEM range at `w2`, only when `flags[3]`. docs/isa.md §MM says: "bit3 `ASCALE` (needs `UNIT` and `ACC`; `ssa` is then the TMEM address…)". So in every valid program `rd[1]` and `rd[3]` are never valid together. No other op writes `rd[3]`. `rd[3]` is a whole footprint range that costs:
- 4 of the 20 pairs per slot: n.wr[0..1] x e.rd[3] and e.wr[0..1] x n.rd[3].
- That is 128 comparators, plus 16 x 65 stored bits.

**Timing.** Area alone is rejected at 104 MHz. The champion's critical path (5.721 ns) is:

IMEM RAMB18 DO (2.55 ns, no output register) -> isel word mux -> `ra` -> R-file mux -> 32-bit add -> `dcmd.w1` -> `p_cmd`

The same shape also exists for ADDI, LOOP and the fetch loop.

Last round's s0 patch (`tools/tourney/runs/otpu_seq/patches/r20260924-001624-s0.patch`, registered `ir` plus an exact one-ahead fetch address `fa`) fixed this:
- logic 5.148 ns, est fmax 114.5 MHz (+10.5%).
- Tests fast, board and perf all passed.
- It was rejected only on area (+1.7%: +322 LUT, +331 FF, +24 LUTRAM).

Its new critical path (build/tourney/otpu_seq/r20260924-001624-s0/otpu_seq/sta.txt) was:

`sunit[9][30]` (a 32-bit `int`) -> `sunit[i] == u` -> cand / oldest -> `start_slot` -> `can_start[4]` -> `ucmd` CE

This proposal pays for the s0 fetch fix with the footprint cut and also shortens that start path.

## Change (rtl/seq/otpu_seq.sv only; otpu_pkg is untouched)

### Part A: registered instruction word (take s0's patch as is)

Apply `r20260924-001624-s0.patch`. It was made against the same champion, 818da9d, so it applies cleanly:
- `ir`/`ir_v`/`fa`/`fa_d`, with cases A–D for the next fetch address.
- The carry-free LOOP zero test.
- The `ifndef SYNTHESIS` `$fatal` that checks `fa` against the old `pc_n` rule.

It was already verified bit-exact (lint; fast 12/12; board 4/4; perf gate passed; 160 nested-loop fuzz programs). The only timing change is +1 cycle at program start.

### Part B: 5-range window footprint

1. Add a module-local type: `typedef struct packed { logic all; rng_t [2:0] rd; rng_t [1:0] wr; } fp5_t;`.
2. Add `function automatic fp5_t fp_pack(input fp_t f)`:
   - Copy `all`, `rd[0..2]` and `wr[0..1]`.
   - If `f.rd[3].v`: if `f.rd[1].v`, set `all = 1`; otherwise `rd[1] = f.rd[3]`.
   - The `all` branch is only reachable for an ISA-invalid ASCALE-without-UNIT MM. It serializes that MM against everything, which is a strict superset of its real dependencies, so it is still correct.
3. Replace `conflict`/`conflict_dram` in the module with one local `function automatic logic [1:0] conf5(input fp5_t n, input fp5_t e)`. It evaluates each of the **16** pair tests once:
   - `hit = a.v && b.v && a.sp == b.sp && a.lo < b.hi && b.lo < a.hi`
   - Pairs: n.wr[i] x e.rd[j<3], e.wr[i] x n.rd[j<3], n.wr[i] x e.wr[j].
   - Bit 1 (`conflict`) = `n.all | e.all | OR(hit)`.
   - Bit 0 (`conflict_dram`) = `n.all | e.all | OR(hit & a.sp == SP_DRAM)`. This is identical to the package's v-masking, because a hit needs `a.sp == b.sp`.
   - Keep plain `<`, so Yosys still uses cmp2lcu, and add no digit loops. The loop total per call is about 16 iterations x 16 slots, far below slang's 4000 unroll limit.
4. Change `c_fp` to `fp5_t`: `c_fp <= fp_pack(fp_ranges(q_cmd, q_pr, D, S))`. Change `sfp[WIN]` to `fp5_t`. `ndep[i]`/`ndepd[i]` = `sv[i] && !fin[i] && conf5(c_fp, sfp[i])[1]` / `[0]`.

**Why this is bit-identical.** For every footprint where `rd[1]` and `rd[3]` are not both valid (all valid programs), the multiset of valid ranges is unchanged; `rd[3]`'s range just moves to slot `rd[1]`.

`conflict` treats all read slots alike: every read slot is paired with the same write slots, and space and validity travel with the range. So `conf5(pack(n), pack(e))` equals `{conflict(n,e), conflict_dram(n,e)}` exactly.

`sdep`/`sdepd`, the starts, the releases and the unit order are all unchanged. In the invalid case the result is a superset of the dependencies. Dependencies only point to older instructions, so this cannot deadlock, and results stay those of sequential execution.

### Part C: one-hot unit tags (timing; small area)

- Carry the unit through P/S/Q/C as `logic [2:0]` instead of `int`. `dunit < 0` is still tested on the `int` from `unit_of` at R.
- Store a per-slot one-hot `logic [NUNITS-1:0] soh [WIN]`, written at dispatch as `1 << c_unit`.
- `sunit[i] == u` becomes `soh[i][u]` in `same_started` and `cand`.
- This is the same function, with no 32-bit compare on the post-A critical path (`sunit` -> `start_slot` -> `can_start`). It also removes the `int` pipeline FFs, up to about 16x29 + 4x29 bits if Yosys has not already merged the sign copies.

## Expected

- **Part B:**
  - About -128 comparators x 22 LUT, plus pair glue, gives about **-2.8 k to -3.0 k LUT**, and -384 CARRY4.
  - FF: -16 x 65 (`sfp` rd[3] lo/hi/v; its `sp` is constant) and -65 (`c_fp`), about **-1.1 k FF**.
  - +~65 LUT for the pack mux (on the n side only, once).
- **Part A:** +322 LUT, +331 FF, +24 LUTRAM (measured).
- **Part C:** about -50 to -150 LUT, and 0 to -500 FF.
- **Net:**
  - LUT about 21.0 k -> 18.2–18.5 k.
  - FF about 10.9 k -> 9.7–10.2 k.
  - Area-eq 29 930 -> about **26.3–27.0 k (-10% to -12%)**.
- **fmax:** Part A alone measured 5.148 ns (114.5 MHz). Part C shortens that path, the comparators' fan-in and OR trees shrink, and Q->C only gains one mux LUT. Expect **est fmax about 114–120 MHz**, which is >= 110.
- **Perf proxy:** +1 cycle at program start (Part A). B and C change nothing in timing.

## Risks

- **Part A** is a large diff. Apply the tested patch verbatim, not a re-derivation, and keep its `$fatal` fetch-address self-check.
- **Missed read slot:** if some op other than MM ever fills `rd[3]`, `fp_pack` still handles it exactly, or with the `all` fallback, because it is generic over `fp_t`. A missed read slot in `conf5` would be a real bug. Every rd index 0..2 must be paired with both n.wr and e.wr.
- **Invalid ASCALE programs:** if the fuzzer emits ASCALE without UNIT, those MMs serialize. Results stay identical, only timing changes, and perf is unaffected because the proxy uses valid programs.
- **Pack mux timing:** `fp_pack` adds one mux level after `fp_ranges`'s adders on Q->C. That path currently sits well below 5 ns in s0's histogram. If it shows up, pack on the S->Q side instead: `rd[3].v` needs only `op`, `flags[3]` and `m != 0`.

Only `rtl/seq/otpu_seq.sv` changed.
- **Part A:** I applied `r20260924-001624-s0.patch` hunk by hand, word for word, because `git apply` needed approval. It adds `ir`/`ir_v`/`fa`/`fa_d`/`ld`, cases A–D, the carry-free `lp_z`, and the `ifndef SYNTHESIS` `$fatal` fetch-address check.

  - `test_mlp_rtl[1]` passed.

title: One-hot oldest-ready select: can_start without the start_slot encode -> sdep/sdepd mux
hypothesis:
# One-hot oldest-ready select: can_start without the start_slot encode -> sdep/sdepd mux

Category: timing

Motivation:
The champion's critical path (5.195 ns, 113 MHz) is no longer on the IMEM fetch loop. It runs
through the per-unit start logic for unit 1 (U_MXU):

    older[11] (FF, 0.40) -> 3 LUT levels (oldest-of-cand test, 1.03..2.53)
      -> start_slot[13] (binary encode, 2.66..2.90)
      -> 3 LUT levels (16:1 mux sdepd[start_slot] & ~same_started, 0/1 reduce, 3.13..3.95)
      -> can_start[1] (4.58) -> 4 x LUT2 (the CE fan-out: sstarted/uq/ucmd/uq_t enables) -> FDRE.CE (5.195)

About 1.7 ns of it (2.90 -> 4.58) is spent turning the oldest candidate into a binary slot id and
then using that id to index sdepd again: a 16:1 x 16-bit mux followed by a zero test. That is
pure encode/decode overhead -- the "is the oldest one ready" bit can be formed per slot in
parallel, from flip-flops only, while the oldest candidate is still being selected. The same
pattern exists for U_COLL (sdep[start_slot]) and, redundantly, for U_DMA/U_Q/U_VPU (their cand
already requires readiness, so the re-check through the mux is logically a no-op but Yosys/ABC
does not know it). Everything else on the histogram is below ~3.75 ns, so removing ~1 ns here
should move the whole design by >= 3% fmax.

Change (rtl/seq/otpu_seq.sv only, the `can_start` / `start_slot` always_comb and the start
block of the always_ff):

1. Per unit, keep `cand` exactly as now and form the one-hot oldest set
   `sel[u][i] = cand[i] && (older[i] & cand) == '0` (already computed inside the loop; just keep
   it as a vector). `start_slot[u]` stays as the binary encode of `sel[u]` (still needed as data
   for `uq[u][...]` and the `scmd` read mux; only D inputs now, not the CE).
2. Per slot, precompute readiness from flops, in parallel with the selection:
   `mrdy[i]  = (sdepd[i] & ~same_started[U_MXU]) == '0`
   `crdy[i]  = (sdep[i]  & ~same_started[U_COLL]) == '0`
3. Replace the check-through-the-mux:
   - U_MXU:  `can_start = |(sel[U_MXU] & mrdy) && urdy && !ustart`
   - U_COLL: `can_start = |(sel[U_COLL] & crdy) && urdy && !ustart`
   - others: `can_start = |cand && urdy && !ustart` (cand[i] already includes
     `(sdep[i] & ~same_started[u]) == 0`, and the selected slot is a member of cand).
   `found` becomes `|cand` (shallow: no older-matrix term).
4. In the start block, set `sstarted[i] <= 1` from `can_start[u] && sel[u][i]` (a per-slot AND)
   instead of the binary decode `sstarted[start_slot[u]]`. `ucmd[u] <= scmd[start_slot[u]]`,
   `uq[u][uq_t] <= start_slot[u]` and the trace keep using start_slot unchanged.

Why bit-identical: the age matrix is a strict total order over valid slots -- at dispatch
`older[free] <= sv` (free is invalid, so no self bit) and column `free` is cleared in every row,
so for any two valid slots exactly one is older than the other, and rows/columns of invalid
slots are masked by cand (which requires sv). Hence for a non-empty cand, `sel` has exactly one
bit, at the slot the current loop picks as start_slot, and `|cand == |sel == found`. So
`|(sel & mrdy) == found && mrdy[start_slot] == found && (sdepd[start_slot] & ~same_started) == 0`,
i.e. can_start, the chosen slot, ucmd, uq and sstarted are the same every cycle as today. No
state, no latency, no protocol change; the Qwen proxy cycle count is unchanged (same start
decisions every cycle). A `ifndef SYNTHESIS` `$onehot0(sel[u])` / `found == |sel[u]` assertion
can guard the invariant in the RTL tests.

Expected:
- fmax: the MXU start path drops from ~10 LUT levels to ~6 (older -> cand&older reduce (2) ->
  sel -> AND-OR with mrdy (2) -> CE fan-out). Estimate 5.2 ns -> ~4.1-4.3 ns for this path; the
  next endpoints (start_slot -> scmd 16:1 mux -> ucmd D, ~3.8-4.0 ns; the 3.3-3.7 ns bulk) then
  set the limit: est fmax ~120-128 MHz (+6..13%).
- LUT: removes two 16:1 x 16-bit muxes + reductions (MXU sdepd, COLL sdep) and three redundant
  ones for the other units that ABC may have kept (~150-300 LUT), adds 32 16-bit AND-reduce
  terms (~3 LUT each, ~100 LUT) and 2 x 16-input AND-OR (~14 LUT). Net ~ -50..-200 LUT (flat to
  -1% area). FF unchanged.

Risks:
- Correctness rests on the one-hot/total-order invariant of `older`; if some path ever left two
  cand members mutually unordered (e.g. `older` rows not rewritten on a re-dispatch), `|sel` could
  differ from the current highest-index pick. The argument above covers dispatch and reset
  (older is only read through cand/sv); the simulation assertion would catch a violation.
- `older` is not reset; in 4-state simulation its unwritten bits are X but are always ANDed with
  cand = 0 there, same as today.
- Yosys may re-share/re-encode the logic and not realise the full gain; if the new critical path
  becomes start_slot -> scmd mux -> ucmd D, a follow-up is a one-hot AND-OR `scmd` read with sel.
implementation:
# One-hot oldest-ready select (rtl/seq/otpu_seq.sv)

- Per unit, the start logic now keeps the oldest-candidate set as a one-hot vector `sel[u]`
  (`cand[i] && (older[i] & cand) == 0`, where `cand` is unchanged). `start_slot[u]` is now the OR-encode of `sel[u]`, which is only
  correct if `sel[u]` is one-hot. It still drives `ucmd`, `uq` and the trace (D inputs only).
- Per-slot readiness `mrdy[i]` (sdepd vs same_started[U_MXU]) and `crdy[i]` (sdep vs
  same_started[U_COLL]) is computed from flops, in parallel with the selection. can_start is
  `|(sel & mrdy)` for the MXU, `|(sel & crdy)` for COLL, and `|cand` for the other units (their cand already
  requires readiness). The sdepd/sdep lookup indexed by `start_slot` is gone.
- `sstarted[i]` is set by `can_start[u] && sel[u][i]` per slot, not by decoding start_slot.
- A new `ifndef SYNTHESIS` check in the always_ff calls `$fatal` if `sel[u]` is not one-hot0 or
  if `|cand != |sel` (the age-matrix total-order invariant everything above depends on).
- Checked: verilator lint is clean. test_mlp_rtl[1], test_scoreboard_stress_single_slice[0],
  test_scoreboard_stress_two_slices[0] and test_fuzz_two_slices[0] pass.
lesson: Oldest-ready select: build per-slot readiness from flops and AND it with the one-hot oldest vector. Skip the binary encode and mux back through start_slot on the CE path. Gain: +20% fmax, ~0 area.

title: Space-segregated scoreboard footprint: 13 range cells per slot instead of 16, no space compares
hypothesis:
# Space-segregated scoreboard footprint: 13 range cells per slot instead of 16, no space compares

Category: area

## Motivation

The scoreboard is the largest block in `otpu_seq`. Every cycle the new instruction's footprint
(`c_fp`) is compared against all WIN=16 slot footprints (`sfp`). Each comparison of two
footprints is `conf5`, which runs 16 range-pair "cells" (`ov`). Each cell does a 2-bit space
equality check, two valid bits and two 32-bit `<` compares. That comes to
16 slots × 16 cells × 2 = 512 32-bit comparators plus 256 space-equality checks, all duplicated
per slot. `sfp` is 16 × 336 = 5376 FFs, which is more than half of the 10182 FFs.

The last accepted round cut the cells from 20 to 16 (MM ASCALE sharing `rd[1]`) and lowered area
by 10.6% (≈3100 area-eq after subtracting the registered IR). So one cell across the window
costs roughly 700–800 area-eq, or about 2.8% of the current 26759. The lesson from that round
also applies here: Yosys already maps `$lt` well, so the lever is fewer range pairs.

A cell is only useful if its two ranges can be in the **same space**. `ov` needs `a.sp == b.sp`.
Today the ranges are stored by role (rd[0..2], wr[0..1]), and any role can hold any space, so
all 16 role pairs must be tested and each test must compare `sp`. If slots are stored **by
space** instead, cross-space pairs are gone by construction. A per-range write bit then removes
the read×read pairs.

What each op actually needs per space (from `fp_ranges`, otpu_pkg.sv):

| op     | DRAM                 | TMEM                                 | ACT |
|--------|----------------------|--------------------------------------|-----|
| LD     | R (rd0)              | W (wr0)                              |     |
| ST     | W (wr0)              | R (rd0)                              |     |
| MM     | R (rd0), R (rd1)     | W (wr0), W (wr1 RMAX), R (rd3 ASCALE)| R (rd2) |
| QACT   |                      | R (rd0), R (rd1), R (rd2)            | W (wr0) |
| QST    | W (wr0), W (wr1)     | R (rd0)                              |     |
| VOP    |                      | W (wr0), R (rd0), R (rd1)            |     |
| GATHER |                      | W (wr0), R (rd0)                     |     |
| BAR    | `all`                |                                      |     |

The new layout:
- DRAM: `d[0]`, `d[1]`, each with a write bit. Pairs d×d: 4 cells.
- TMEM: `t[0]`, `t[1]`, each with a write bit, and `t[2]`, which is **always a read** (MM
  ASCALE, the third QACT read, the second VOP read). Pairs t×t minus (t2,t2): 8 cells.
- ACT: one range `a` with a write bit. 1 cell. ACT addresses are narrow: lo is 8 bits
  (`w6[31:24]` / `w2[15:8]`) and hi = lo + kb ≤ 255 + 65535 < 2^17. So this cell is two
  17-bit compares, not two 32-bit ones.

That gives 13 cells, of which 12 are 32-bit, instead of 16 × 32-bit. There are no `sp` fields
or space compares, and the DRAM-only part for the MXU stream start (`ndepd`) is just the OR of
the 4 DRAM cells.

## Change (rtl/seq/otpu_seq.sv only)

1. Replace `fp5_t` / `fp_pack` / `conf5` with:
   ```systemverilog
   typedef struct packed { logic v, w; logic [31:0] lo, hi; } r32w_t;   // DRAM/TMEM, R or W
   typedef struct packed { logic v;    logic [31:0] lo, hi; } r32_t;    // TMEM t[2]: read only
   typedef struct packed {
     logic            all;
     r32w_t [1:0]     d;        // DRAM
     r32w_t [1:0]     t;        // TMEM (may be written)
     r32_t            t2;       // TMEM (read only)
     logic            av, aw;   // ACT: [alo, ahi), ahi < 2^17
     logic [7:0]      alo;
     logic [16:0]     ahi;
   } fps_t;
   ```
   `fp_seg(cmd op, fp_t f)` is a per-op `case` that routes the fixed `fp_ranges` fields as in
   the table above. It copies `v/lo/hi`, sets `w` for ranges taken from `wr[*]`, and drops `sp`.
   It is pure wiring plus an op-keyed mux on `q_cmd.op`, which is a flop, so the decode runs in
   parallel with the `fp_ranges` adders. It replaces `fp_pack` at the Q→C register:
   `c_fp <= fp_seg(q_cmd.op, fp_ranges(q_cmd, q_pr, D, S))`.
   The `all` fallback for the invalid ASCALE && !UNIT MM goes away: its DRAM `rd1` and TMEM
   `rd3` now get separate slots (`d[1]`, `t2`).

2. `conf_s(n, e)` returns `{any, dram}`:
   - `any = dram = n.all | e.all`
   - DRAM: for i,j∈{0,1}, `n.d[i].v & e.d[j].v & (n.d[i].w | e.d[j].w) & n.d[i].lo < e.d[j].hi & e.d[j].lo < n.d[i].hi`
     sets both `any` and `dram`.
   - TMEM: the same on {t[0], t[1], t2}² minus (t2, t2), with t2's write bit fixed at 0. Sets `any`.
   - ACT: `n.av & e.av & (n.aw | e.aw) & n.alo < e.ahi & e.alo < n.ahi` (17-bit, alo
     zero-extended). Sets `any`.

   `ndep`/`ndepd`, `sfp`, `c_fp` just change type. Nothing else in the window, start logic,
   or fetch changes.

3. Simulation-only checks (`ifndef SYNTHESIS`, at the Q stage): the number of valid ranges in
   `fp_t` must equal the number in `fps_t` (nothing dropped by the routing), every routed range
   must have the expected `sp`, and the ACT `hi[31:17]` / `lo[31:8]` must be 0.

### Why results stay bit-identical (and cycles too)

The original package `conflict(n,e)` tests every (write of one, read-or-write of the other)
range pair with `ov`, which requires the same space. The segregated form tests exactly the set
of same-space pairs where at least one side is a write. Cross-space pairs are always false in
`ov`, and read×read pairs were never tested. So `any` equals `conflict(fp_n, fp_e)` and `dram`
equals `conflict_dram(fp_n, fp_e)`, bit for bit, for every valid program. That matches the
current `conf5` too, which only differs for the invalid ASCALE && !UNIT MM (where it used
`all`, a superset). The ACT narrowing is exact because the values fit in 8/17 bits, and `ov`
compares zero-extended values the same way. The dependency matrices, and therefore every start,
release, completion and the perf-proxy cycle count, are unchanged. Unit commands and all port
protocols are untouched.

## Expected

- Comparator logic: 16 → 12 full cells + 1 half-width cell, about −22% of the cell compares.
  The 256 space-equality checks and the `dram |= sp == SP_DRAM` gating are gone, and the OR
  trees behind `ndep`/`ndepd` are shallower.
  Estimate: **−1500 to −2500 LUT** (about 3 cells × ~16 slots at ~30–50 LUT per cell per
  slot, calibrated on the 20→16 round, plus the half-width ACT cell and the sp checks).
- FF: each slot grows 336 → 357 bits (write bits, the t2 split, the narrow ACT range):
  +21 × 17 (16 slots + `c_fp`) ≈ **+360 FF** (+180 area-eq). The routing mux: about +100 LUT.
- Net: **about −5% area-equivalent** (at least −3% even if cells cost half the calibration).
- fmax: neutral or slightly better. The critical path (older → start_slot → can_start → CE,
  5.195 ns) is untouched. The scoreboard path (`c_fp`/`sfp` → compares → `ndep` → `sdep`)
  gets a shallower OR tree. The Q-stage path gains at most one mux level after the
  `fp_ranges` adders, and it has ample slack (the histogram puts most endpoints < 3.5 ns).

## Risks

- **Routing mistakes** (e.g. a range dropped or sent to the wrong space) would give missing
  dependencies and wrong results. The sim-only count/space asserts catch this on every
  instruction in the RTL tests.
- **Missing a write bit** would silently drop a RAW/WAR dependency. The per-op table is small,
  and the `all`/count assertions plus bit-exact tests over MM (ACC/RMAX/ASCALE), QACT
  (CSCALE/RSCALE), QST, VOP binary modes and GATHER cover it.
- **A future op with more ranges per space** (e.g. 4 TMEM ranges, or 2 TMEM writes plus 2
  reads) would not fit. The assertion fires in simulation, and the fallback is `all` for that
  case.
- **Unroll limits** (lesson s1): the loops are only 16 slots × 13 cells of plain `<`, far below
  slang's limit. No digit loops.
- **Yosys could share less than expected** if it had already pruned impossible cross-space
  pairs through constant propagation. It can't, because `sp` is a runtime register field in
  `sfp`, so the saving is real.
implementation:
# Space-segregated scoreboard footprint (rtl/seq/otpu_seq.sv)

- Replaced `fp5_t`/`fp_pack`/`conf5` with `fps_t` (DRAM `d[0..1]` + TMEM `t[0..1]`, each with a write bit; read-only TMEM `t2`; one narrow ACT range `av/aw/alo[7:0]/ahi[16:0]`), `fp_seg(op, fp_t)` (a per-op `case` routing following the HYPOTHESIS table; MM rd3 (ASCALE), QACT rd2 (RSCALE) and VOP rd1 go to `t2`), and `conf_s` (13 cells: 4 DRAM, 8 TMEM (t×t, t×t2, t2×t; the t2 pairs need the other side's write bit), 1 ACT of 8/17-bit compares). `dram` is set only by the DRAM cells; `all` sets both outputs, as before.
- `c_fp <= fp_seg(q_cmd.op, fp_ranges(...))`. `sfp`/`c_fp` change type, and `conf5` becomes `conf_s` in the `ndep` loop. Nothing else changes (window, start, release, fetch, ports).
- The `all` fallback for an invalid MM (ASCALE && !UNIT) is gone: its DRAM rd1 and TMEM rd3 now get separate slots (`d[1]`, `t2`), which is exact.
- Sim-only (`ifndef SYNTHESIS`) check at Q→C: `fp_seg_ok` confirms `all` matches and the number of valid ranges is equal. It also confirms each valid source range shows up in its own space with the same lo/hi and the right read/write bit, and that ACT `lo[31:8]`/`hi[31:17]` are 0. If any of this fails it calls `$fatal`. Because it calls `fp_ranges` again (sim only), synthesis is unaffected.
- A small helper `ovs(av, alo, ahi, bv, blo, bhi)` holds one cell's compare. The write-bit condition goes into its first valid argument.
- Checked: Verilator lint (the given flags) is clean. `test_mlp_rtl[1]` passes, and so do the 20 `fuzz_single_slice`/`scoreboard_stress_single_slice` tests. Full gates and synthesis numbers have not been run.
lesson: Storing scoreboard slots by space (DRAM 2, TMEM 2+always-read t2, ACT narrow 17-bit) instead of by role cut cells 16→13 and dropped all sp compares: area -8.2%. Fewer range pairs is still the lever.

title: Loop-stack predicates as flops: per-entry `rem > 1` / `rem > 2` flags and per-entry `stk_end` compares on the fetch-address path
hypothesis:
# Loop-stack predicates as flops: per-entry `rem > 1` / `rem > 2` flags and per-entry `stk_end` compares on the fetch-address path

Category: timing

## Motivation
The critical path (4.27 ns, est. 136 MHz) ends at the IMEM read address (`fa_d[9]` -> RAMB18
ADDR). It starts at the loop stack's trip count:

    stk_rem (FDRE) -> LUT6.I0 -> LUT6.I0   (4:1 mux stk_rem[sp-1], 2 x ~0.64 ns)
                   -> CARRY4 S->CO -> CI->O (`stk_rem[..] > 1/2` mapped as a subtract chain, ~0.77 ns)
                   -> 9 LUTs (hit priority B/C/D -> succ -> fa_d)
                   -> imem ADDR

About 2 ns of the 4.27 ns (mux, mux, carry) is only there to work out "is the top count > 1 / > 2"
and "is the second count > 1" (branches B, C and D of `hit`). These are 32-bit values read through
an `sp-1` / `sp-2` mux and compared with a carry chain in the same cycle that has to produce the
RAM address. The same `fa_d` cone also has two more stack paths of the same shape:
`stk_end[sp-1] == fa` / `stk_end[sp-2] == fa` (hit1/hit2) and `stk_end[sp-1] == pc` (at_end). Each is a
32-bit 4:1 mux (2 slow LUT6.I0 levels) followed by a 32-bit equality. In the histogram they are
the lone endpoints between 3.5 and 4.1 ns, above the ~500 scoreboard endpoints at 3.3–3.5 ns.
Branch A also compares `lp_cnt` (`!= 0`, `> 1`) and `lp_len` (`== 1`) as 32-bit values on this path.
All of these are functions of flip-flops that change at most once per LOOP or loop end, so they
can be computed when the stack is written instead of when it is read.

## Change (rtl/seq/otpu_seq.sv only)
1. **Per-entry count flags.** Add `logic stk_g1 [4], stk_g2 [4];` with the invariant
   `stk_g1[k] == (stk_rem[k] > 1)` and `stk_g2[k] == (stk_rem[k] > 2)` for every live entry
   (`k < sp`). Keep them next to `stk_rem`, and write them wherever `stk_rem` is written:
   - push (LOOP second cycle, count != 0): `stk_g1[sp] <= lp_g1; stk_g2[sp] <= lp_g2;`
   - decrement in `advance()` (the top has rem > 1): `stk_g1[sp-1] <= stk_g2[sp-1];`
     `stk_g2[sp-1] <= |stk_rem[sp-1][31:2];` because (rem-1 > 1) == (rem > 2) and
     (rem-1 > 2) == (rem > 3) == |rem[31:2]. This is on the flop D side, off the fetch path. It can
     be written per entry (`for k: if (k == sp-1) ... |stk_rem[k][31:2]`) so no mux is needed.
   - a pop leaves the entry below unchanged, and its flags stay valid.
   Replace every `stk_rem[sp-1] > 1` with `top_g1`, `stk_rem[sp-1] > 2` with `top_g2`, and
   `stk_rem[sp-2] > 1` with `sec_g1`. This covers `hit` D/B/C and the test in `advance()`.
   `top_g1 = |(g1_vec & top_oh)` etc., where `top_oh[k] = (sp == k+1)` and `sec_oh[k] = (sp == k+2)`
   are decoded from the 3-bit `sp`. Each is then a single 1-bit AND-OR (1 LUT) instead of
   mux + mux + carry chain. `stk_rem` stays 32 bits because it still counts.
2. **LOOP registers' flags.** At the LOOP's first cycle, also register `lp_nz <= !lp_z` (already
   computed), `lp_len1 <= (iw[1] == 1)` and `lp_g1 <= !lp_z && !lp_one`. `lp_one` is the
   carry-free "a + b == 1" test, like the existing `lp_z` (a + b == K iff
   `(a ^ b ^ K) == (c << 1)` where `c_i = K_i ? a_i & b_i : a_i | b_i`). It is not
   `(rv(ra)+iw[2]) > 1`, because that would put an OR-reduce after the 32-bit carry chain that
   already feeds `lp_cnt`. `lp_g2 = |lp_cnt[31:2] || &lp_cnt[1:0]` is computed at the push from
   the `lp_cnt` flop (D side, cheap). Branch A becomes `if (lp_nz) begin hit = lp_len1 && lp_g1; ...`,
   and the push condition `lp_cnt != 0` becomes `lp_nz`.
3. **Per-entry end compares.** Compute `efa[k] = (stk_end[k] == fa)` and `epc[k] = (stk_end[k] == pc)`
   for k = 0..3 in parallel. Then `hit1 = |(efa & top_oh)`, `hit2 = |(efa & sec_oh)` and
   `at_end = |(epc & top_oh)`. The `sp` select moves after the comparators and becomes a 1-bit
   AND-OR, which removes the two LUT6.I0 mux levels before each 32-bit equality. Area is about the
   same: 8 comparators replace 3 comparators plus three 32-bit 4:1 muxes. `sp != 0` and `sp >= 2`
   are then implied by the one-hot vectors.
4. Keep the existing `ifndef SYNTHESIS` next-pc `$fatal` check. Add one that checks, for every
   `k < sp`, that `stk_g1[k] == (stk_rem[k] > 1)`, `stk_g2[k] == (stk_rem[k] > 2)`, and that
   `lp_nz/lp_g1/lp_len1` match `lp_cnt/lp_len` while `lp` is set. Any flag bug then fails the
   RTL tests immediately.

**Why results stay bit-identical:** each new signal equals the expression it replaces for every
reachable state. The flags are updated in the same cycle as `stk_rem`, and from the same
condition, so the invariant holds after every edge. The one-hot selects equal the `sp-1` / `sp-2`
indexing for `sp <= 4`. The ISA limits nesting to depth 4, and `isasim.py` raises "loop stack
overflow" beyond it, so no valid program has `sp > 4`. Nothing about fetch order, `ld`, the
dispatch pipeline, the window or any port changes. The cycle-by-cycle behaviour (and so the
Qwen3 proxy) is identical, not just the results.

## Expected
- fmax: the current worst path loses about 2 ns (mux+mux+carry replaced by one ~0.3–0.6 ns LUT),
  and the stk_end-compare paths lose about 1.3 ns each. The worst `fa_d` path should drop to
  about 3.4–3.8 ns, with the scoreboard floor (3.3–3.5 ns) or the LOOP-skip adder
  `pc+1+iw[1]` / `lp_z` becoming critical. Est. fmax 136 → ~150–160 MHz (+10 to +18%).
- FF: +8 (stk_g1/g2) + 3 (lp_nz, lp_g1, lp_len1) = about +11.
- LUT: about -30 to +20. Removed: 3 x 32-bit stk_rem compare chains, the `stk_rem[sp-2]` mux,
  two lp_cnt compares, and three 32-bit stk_end muxes. Added: 5 comparators, flag
  update/select logic and `lp_one`. Area-equivalent change is well under +0.2%, inside the
  "+3% fmax at <= +1% area" acceptance rule.

## Risks
- A missed `stk_rem` write site leaves the flags stale, so loop ends go wrong. Covered by the new
  simulation invariant check and by the loop tests in tests/test_rtl.py.
- The `lp_one` identity must be written exactly (bit 0 uses `a & b`, higher bits `a | b`, carry-out
  of bit 31 dropped). An error only affects one-instruction loop bodies (branch A with
  `lp_len == 1`) and is caught by the existing next-pc `$fatal` check.
- Out-of-range `sp` (> 4) now reads as "no hit" instead of X. This only happens in programs that
  the ISA and ISS reject.
- The gain may be capped by the next `fa_d` path (the R-file mux into `lp_z`, or the
  `pc + 1 + iw[1]` skip adder), which we cannot see in the single-path report. The change still
  removes the top ~0.5 ns slice of the cone at no area cost.
implementation:
# Loop-stack predicates as flops (rtl/seq/otpu_seq.sv)

- Added per-entry `stk_g1[4]`/`stk_g2[4]` (== `stk_rem[k] > 1` / `> 2` for live entries). They are written at the push (`lp_g1`, `|lp_cnt[31:2] || &lp_cnt[1:0]`) and at the decrement in `advance()`, which is now a per-entry loop over `top_oh`: `g1 <= g2`, `g2 <= |rem[31:2]`, `rem <= rem - 1`. A pop leaves the entry below unchanged.
- `top_oh[k] = (sp == k+1)` and `sec_oh[k] = (sp == k+2)` give 1-bit AND-OR selects `top_g1`, `top_g2` and `sec_g1`. These replace every `stk_rem[sp-1] > 1/2` and `stk_rem[sp-2] > 1` in `hit` (branches D/B/C) and in `advance()`.
- `efa[k] = stk_end[k] == fa` and `epc[k] = stk_end[k] == pc` are computed for all 4 entries. `hit1`, `hit2` and `at_end` are now `|(efa/epc & top_oh/sec_oh)`, which also covers the `sp != 0` and `sp >= 2` guards.
- The LOOP's first cycle also registers `lp_nz = !lp_z`, `lp_g1 = !lp_z && !lp_one` and `lp_len1 = (iw[1] == 1)`. `lp_one` is the carry-free "a + b == 1" identity: `(a^b^1) == (c<<1)`, where `c = {a[31:1]|b[31:1], a[0]&b[0]}`. Branch A and the push condition now use these flags.
- `hit_pc` still reads `stk_start[sp-1]` and `stk_start[sp-2]` through the `sp` mux, as before. The hypothesis did not ask to change that.
- New `ifndef SYNTHESIS` `$fatal` checks: the flags of every live entry match `stk_rem`, and `lp_nz`/`lp_g1`/`lp_len1` match `lp_cnt`/`lp_len` while `lp` is set. The existing next-pc check still uses the raw `stk_rem`/`lp_cnt` compares, so it stays an independent reference.
- Verification: the Verilator lint is clean. These tests pass: `test_mlp_rtl[1]` and `[2]`, `test_attention_layer_rtl`, `test_fuzz_single_slice[0-7]` and `test_fuzz_two_slices[0]`. A dedicated test of nested loops with one-instruction bodies was not run, because I could not place a scratch file without writing outside the allowed paths. The `$fatal` invariants cover those cases in the full gates.
lesson: otpu_seq: precomputing loop-stack predicates (rem>1/>2 flags, per-entry compares) on the fa_d path gave only +1.3% fmax at +0.5% area; the ~500 scoreboard endpoints at 3.3–3.5 ns cap the gain.

title: Per-unit command read straight from the window's LUT-RAM (drop the 5 x 240-bit ucmd registers)
hypothesis:
# Per-unit command read straight from the window's LUT-RAM (drop the 5 x 240-bit ucmd registers)
Category: area

Motivation:
The champion has FF 10182 and LUT-RAM 872. `scmd[WIN]` (16 x 240 bits, 5 async read ports)
is the 872 LUT-RAM. Each start copies `scmd[start_slot[u]]` into `ucmd[u]`, a 240-bit FDRE
register per unit: 5 x 240 = 1200 FFs, about 12% of all FFs and ~600 area-equivalent (2.2% of
26789). These registers only hold a copy of data that is already stored, unchanged, in `scmd`:
a slot's `scmd` entry is written once at dispatch (`c_go`, into a free slot) and cannot be
rewritten until the slot completes (`fin` -> `sv` clear). So while a unit is working on a slot,
`scmd[slot]` is stable and is exactly the value `ucmd[u]` holds.

Change (rtl/seq/otpu_seq.sv only):
1. Add `logic [SW-1:0] ucs [NUNITS];`, the slot each unit last started. In the start loop,
   replace `ucmd[u] <= scmd[start_slot[u]];` with `ucs[u] <= start_slot[u];`. It is registered
   on the same edge as `ustart[u]`, as `ucmd[u]` is today.
2. Drive the output combinationally from the LUT-RAM:
   `always_comb for (int u = 0; u < NUNITS; u++) ucmd[u] = scmd[ucs[u]];`

- Out-of-context the units' paths now start at a LUT-RAM async read (ucs FF -> RAM32M ~1 ns)

  board's coll_cmd passthrough).
- Before the first start, `ucmd` shows scmd[0] (uninitialised) instead of the uninitialised

- Verilator lint: `ucmd` moves from always_ff to always_comb. There is one driver per element,

title: Loop-stack predicates as per-entry flag flops: no compare or stack mux on the IMEM address path

# Loop-stack predicates as per-entry flag flops: no compare or stack mux on the IMEM address path

Category: timing

## Motivation

The champion's critical path (4.381 ns, est. 133 MHz) is the fetch-address loop:

    stk_rem FF -> LUT6 (sp-1 mux) -> LUT6 -> CARRY4 x2 (stk_rem[sp-1] > 1 / > 2)
      -> 9 LUT levels (hit case mux B/C/D, succ = hit ? hit_pc : fa+1, fa_d mux) -> RAMB18 ADDR

That is 2.45 ns before the hit logic even starts. `hit` also needs three sp-muxed 32-bit
equality compares, all computed from flops in the same cycle:
`hit1 = stk_end[sp-1] == fa`, `hit2 = stk_end[sp-2] == fa`, and `at_end = stk_end[sp-1] == pc`
(the last one picks the B/C case). Each is a 4:1 mux (LUT6 on a slow pin), then XOR, then a 3-level AND tree.

r20260924-010905-s0 replaced only the `rem > 1/2` compares with flops and gained just +1.3%.
It left the sp-muxed `stk_end` equality compares on `hit`, and those are about as deep as the
compare it removed. To make the address path short, *every* loop-stack predicate that `hit`
reads has to come straight from a flop. `fa_d` also drives every IMEM RAMB18 address pin (about
57 BRAMs x 10 bits), so it probably accounts for most of the 3.0-3.4 ns histogram bulk as well.

## Change (rtl/seq/otpu_seq.sv only)

Keep `stk_start/stk_end/stk_rem/sp` as they are. Add per-entry predicate flops (k = 0..3). Each one
keeps an exact invariant, updated at the same edges that change its operands:

| flop | invariant (for valid entries k < sp) |
|---|---|
| `e_eq[k]` | `stk_end[k] == fa` |
| `a_eq[k]` | `stk_end[k] == pc` |
| `g1[k]`, `g2[k]` | `stk_rem[k] > 1`, `stk_rem[k] > 2` |
| `se[k][j]` (k <= j) | `stk_end[k] == stk_start[j]` |
| `lp_len1`, `lp_len2`, `lp_nz` | `lp_len == 1`, `lp_len == 2`, `lp_cnt != 0` (set in the LOOP's first cycle from `iw[1]` and `!lp_z`) |

The fetch logic then reads the flags:
`hit1 = sp!=0 && e_eq[sp-1]`, `hit2 = sp>=2 && e_eq[sp-2]`, `at_end = sp!=0 && a_eq[sp-1]`,
`tg1/tg2 = g1/g2[sp-1]`, `ng1 = g1[sp-2]`, case A `hit = lp_len1 && lp_cnt > 1` under `lp_nz`.
The case structure of `hit` / `hit_pc` / `succ` / `fa_d` and the `ld` / `adv` logic stay exactly as
they are. Only the leaf predicates change: they become flops through a 7-input sp select, with no
compare and no 32-bit mux. `advance()` uses `tg1` instead of `stk_rem[sp-1] > 1`.

### Flag next-state (all compares move to flop D-paths, off the BRAM address)

Three comparator sets, each 4 plain 32-bit equalities placed after adders that already exist:
- `C1[k] = stk_end[k] == fa + 1`, where `fa + 1` is the `succ` incrementer.
- `C3[k] = stk_end[k] == pc + 1`.
- `C2[k] = stk_end[k] == pc + 1 + iw[1]`, the skip target already computed for `fa_d`. Write it as one
  carry chain, `({pc,1'b1} + {iw[1],1'b1}) >> 1`.

`e_eq'[k]`, following the same case split that picks `fa_d`:
- `rst`: 0
- LOOP first cycle (`lpf`): `lp_z ? C2[k] : C3[k]`. The stack is unchanged and `fa' = pc+1(+iw1)`.
- `ld && hit`:
  - case A: `e_eq[k]`, because `fa' = fa`.
  - D/B: `se[k][sp-1]`.
  - C: `se[k][sp-2]`.
- `ld && !hit`: `C1[k]`.
- Otherwise: hold.

Override for the entry being pushed (`ld && ir_v && op==LOOP && lp && lp_nz`, k = sp). In the
LOOP's second cycle `fa == pc+1`, so `stk_end[p] = pc + lp_len` gives `e_eq'[p] = hit ? lp_len1 : lp_len2`.

`a_eq'[k]` (pc' = fa at `ld`):
- `ld`: `e_eq[k]`, with the pushed entry getting `lp_len1`.
- Otherwise: hold.

Push p:
- `se[k][p] <= e_eq[k]` for k < p. This is `stk_end[k] == fa == pc+1 == stk_start[p]`.
- `se[p][p] <= lp_len1`.
- `g1[p] <= lp_cnt > 1`, `g2[p] <= lp_cnt > 2`.

Decrement of the top t:
- `g1[t] <= g2[t]`
- `g2[t] <= stk_rem[t] > 3`, computed from the existing `stk_rem[sp-1]` mux that feeds the decrement.

Pop needs no update: the entries below keep their invariants because their ends and starts do not
move, and `e_eq` / `a_eq` track fa / pc for every live entry.

### Why results stay bit-identical

`hit`, `hit_pc`, `succ`, `fa_d`, `ld` and the stack updates are the same Boolean functions of the
same state. Each replaced subterm (for example `stk_end[sp-1] == fa`) becomes a flop that holds
exactly that value, by the invariants above. For every way `fa`, `pc` or an entry can change
(reset, LOOP first cycle, `ld` with or without a hit in cases A/B/C/D, push, decrement, pop, hold),
the next-state rule recomputes the equality against the new operand. The fetch sequence and cycle
timing are therefore unchanged: same pc stream, same dispatch cycles, and the same perf-proxy cycle
count. Nothing changes at the unit or loader ports.

Add a simulation-only check (`ifndef SYNTHESIS`, next to the existing next_pc `$fatal`): for k < sp,
assert that `e_eq[k] == (stk_end[k]==fa)`, `a_eq[k] == (stk_end[k]==pc)`, `g1/g2` match `stk_rem`,
and `se[k][j]` matches. The fuzz and scoreboard-stress tests then catch any missed update case.

## Expected

- **fa_d cone:** from about 13 levels (including 2.45 ns of slow-pin mux and carry) to about 6-7 LUT levels.
  - flag select (2) -> hit case (1-2) -> succ (1) -> fa_d (1-2)
  - The worst side inputs are `ld` (sv -> have_free -> r_take -> adv: about 6 levels) and `lp_z` (R mux + zero detect, which enters only the last mux level).
  - Estimated arrival about 2.6-3.0 ns at the BRAM address.
- **New critical path:** whatever is next, probably scoreboard / C-stage endpoints at about 3.4-3.8 ns. The flag D-paths are at most about 2.9 ns (the 32-bit incrementer or adder, then equality, then a 2-level mux).
- **Est fmax:** about 133 -> 150-165 MHz (+12% to +24%). The +3% bar has a wide margin.
- **Area:**
  - Removed: the stk_end sp-1 and sp-2 muxes (about 64 LUTs), 3 equality compares, the stk_rem sp-2 mux, and the > 1 / > 2 carry compares (about 150 LUTs in total).
  - Added: 12 equality comparators (about 156 LUTs), flag next-state logic (about 40 LUTs) and about 32 FFs.
  - Net: about +50-80 LUTs, +32 FFs, which is about +0.3% area-eq (limit +1%).
  - LUT-RAM, DSP and BRAM unchanged.

## Risks

- **A missed flag update case** gives wrong loop control, which shows up as a test mismatch or a hang. Mitigations:
  - The sim-only invariant asserts and the existing next_pc `$fatal` fire at the first divergence.
  - The trickiest cases:
    - The pushed entry: `lp_len1/2`, `se` column p, and its `a_eq`.
    - Case C (pop, then loop back to `stk_start[sp-2]`): uses `se[k][sp-2]`.
    - The LOOP first cycle when `fa != pc+1`: this is why C3 compares against `pc+1`, not `fa`.
- **Reset:** `sp=0` makes every flag unused, but still reset `e_eq` / `a_eq` to 0 to keep lint and X-propagation clean.
- **ABC could restructure the smaller cone poorly.** The flags remove carry chains and slow-pin muxes outright, so the logic depth drops even so.
- **Invalid programs** (depth > 4, a body ending on its enclosing body's last instruction) behave as before only as far as the current RTL defines them. The flags track exact equalities, so even those cases follow the same compares.

# Space-segregated scoreboard footprint on the current champion: 13 cells instead of 16, no space compares, valid bits folded into `hi`

Category: area

## Motivation

The scoreboard is most of `otpu_seq`. At C, the new footprint `c_fp` is checked against all 16
slot footprints `sfp[i]` with `conf5`, which uses 16 range-pair cells (`ov`). Each cell has two
valid bits, a 2-bit space equality and two 32-bit `<` compares. Across the window that is 256
cells: 512 32-bit comparators plus 256 space compares, and it accounts for most of the 18169 LUTs
and 1933 CARRY4s. `sfp` is 16 × 336 = 5376 of the 9002 FFs.

Round r20260924-005905-s1 tested this exact lever: store each slot's ranges by space (DRAM /
TMEM / ACT) with a write bit, so cross-space pairs and read×read pairs are never built. It passed
every gate (lint, fast, board, perf 1912272 cycles, identical) and gave area −8.2% (LUT → 15793) at
120 MHz. It was marked "improvement" but not merged, because the same round merged the one-hot
select (s0). The champion has changed since then only in the start select (d946609) and in the ucmd
LUT-RAM read (11657d1). Neither touches `fp5_t`, `conf5`, `sfp` or `c_fp`, so the saving should
carry over almost fully. LESSONS: "fewer range pairs is still the lever". This proposal ports that
change and also removes most of its FF cost (+21 FF/slot last time).

## Change (rtl/seq/otpu_seq.sv only)

1. **Replace `fp5_t` / `fp_pack` / `conf5`** with a space-segregated layout:
   ```systemverilog
   typedef struct packed { logic w; logic [31:0] lo, hi; } r32w_t;  // TMEM, read or write
   typedef struct packed { logic [31:0] lo, hi; } r32_t;            // DRAM range / TMEM read-only
   typedef struct packed {
     logic            all;
     logic            dw;        // the DRAM ranges are writes (both are, or neither is)
     r32_t  [1:0]     d;         // DRAM
     r32w_t [1:0]     t;         // TMEM, may be written
     r32_t            t2;        // TMEM, always a read (MM ASCALE, QACT RSCALE, VOP operand b)
     logic            aw;        // ACT: [alo, ahi), ahi < 2^17
     logic [7:0]      alo;
     logic [16:0]     ahi;
   } fps_t;
   ```
   **No valid bits.** An invalid range is stored with `hi = 0`. This is exact:
   `ov(a,b) = a.v & b.v & a.lo < b.hi & b.lo < a.hi`. If `a.hi == 0`, then `b.lo < 0` is false,
   and symmetrically for `b`, so `hi' = v ? hi : 0` gives the same result as the explicit `v`
   terms, including valid ranges whose `lo + len` wraps to 0 (already non-overlapping). Unset
   ranges from `fp_ranges` are `'0`, so they are invalid already.
   **One DRAM write bit.** Two DRAM ranges only occur in MM (both reads) and QST (both writes).
   LD and ST have one. So `d[0].w == d[1].w` whenever both are valid.

2. **`fp_seg(op, fp_t f)`**, an op-keyed `case` on `q_cmd.op` (a flop), used at the Q→C register
   instead of `fp_pack`: `c_fp <= fp_seg(q_cmd.op, fp_ranges(q_cmd, q_pr, D, S))`. The routing
   follows `fp_ranges` (otpu_pkg.sv):

   | op | d (dw) | t[0] | t[1] | t2 | ACT |
   |---|---|---|---|---|---|
   | LD | rd0 (R) | wr0 W | | | |
   | ST | wr0 (W) | rd0 R | | | |
   | MM | rd0, rd1 (R) | wr0 W | wr1 W (RMAX) | rd3 (ASCALE) | rd2 (R) |
   | QACT | | rd0 R | rd1 R (CSCALE) | rd2 (RSCALE) | wr0 (W) |
   | QST | wr0, wr1 (W) | rd0 R | | | |
   | VOP | | wr0 W | rd0 R | rd1 | |
   | GATHER | | wr0 W | rd0 R | | |
   | BAR | `all` | | | | |

   Each routed range stores `lo` and `v ? hi : 0`. ACT stores `lo[7:0]` and `hi[16:0]`. `lo` is
   `w6[31:24]` or `w2[15:8]` (8 bits), and `hi = lo + kb` with a 16-bit `kb` is below 2^17, so the
   truncation is exact.

3. **`conf_s(n, e)` → `{any, dram}`**, 13 cells:
   - DRAM, 4 cells: `(n.dw | e.dw) & n.d[i].lo < e.d[j].hi & e.d[j].lo < n.d[i].hi`, for
     i, j ∈ {0,1}. Each cell sets `any` and `dram`.
   - TMEM, 8 cells: t[i]×t[j] with `(n.t[i].w | e.t[j].w)`, t[i]×e.t2 with `n.t[i].w`, and
     n.t2×e.t[i] with `e.t[i].w`. Each cell sets `any`.
   - ACT, 1 cell (8/17-bit): `(n.aw | e.aw) & {9'b0,n.alo} < e.ahi & {9'b0,e.alo} < n.ahi`. Sets `any`.
   - `any = dram = n.all | e.all` as before.

   `ndep`/`ndepd`, `sfp` and `c_fp` only change type. Nothing else changes: window, age matrix,
   start/release, fetch, ucmd, ports.

4. **Simulation-only equivalence check** (`ifndef SYNTHESIS`). This is stronger than last time:
   keep a shadow `fp_t sfp_ref[WIN]` and `c_ref`, written wherever `sfp`/`c_fp` are. At every
   cycle with `c_v`, `$fatal` unless, for every valid slot `i`,
   `conf_s(c_fp, sfp[i]) == {conflict(c_ref, sfp_ref[i]), conflict_dram(c_ref, sfp_ref[i])}`
   (the package reference functions). Also assert that ACT `lo[31:8]` and `hi[31:17]` are 0 at
   Q→C. Any routing or write-bit mistake then fails the RTL tests immediately, not just when it
   happens to change a result.

### Why results stay bit-identical

`ov` is false across spaces. The package's `conflict()` tests every (write, read-or-write) pair
and never read×read. The segregated form tests exactly the same-space pairs where at least one
side is a write, and folding `v` into `hi` is exact (shown above). So `any` equals `conflict()`
and `dram` equals `conflict_dram()` bit for bit. The current `conf5` equals them too, except for
the invalid MM with ASCALE and without UNIT, where it uses `all` (a superset). The new form is
exact there as well, and it only changes scheduling, never data. The dependency matrices, and
therefore every start, release and completion, are the same as today on every valid program. The
perf proxy should give the same cycle count (the last run: 1912272, identical to the champion's).

## Expected

- LUT: about −2300 to −2600. That is 3 of the 16 32-bit cells gone, one cell becomes 17-bit, and
  all 256 space compares and the `sp == SP_DRAM` gating go too. Calibration from 005905-s1:
  ~−2400 LUT.
- FF per slot: 1 + 1 + 2·64 + 2·65 + 64 + 1 + 8 + 17 = **350 vs 336 now** (last time 357).
  +14 × 17 ≈ **+240 FF** (+120 area-eq). The routing mux adds about +100 LUT.
- Area-equivalent: 26142 → about **23.9k (−8 to −9%)**. The accept bar is −1%, so the margin is
  wide.
- fmax: about neutral (≥ 125 MHz, target 110). The critical path (stk_rem → fa_d → IMEM
  address) is untouched. The scoreboard compare → ndep → sdep path gets a shallower OR tree.
  The Q→C path gains at most one op-keyed mux level after the `fp_ranges` adders, and that mux
  can merge with `fp_ranges`' own op case.

## Risks

- **Routing mistakes** (a range dropped, sent to the wrong space, or given the wrong write bit)
  would miss dependencies and give wrong results. The sim-only `conflict()` shadow check catches
  them the first time the pair is compared.
- **`hi = 0` folding:** it must apply to every routed range, including ACT (`ahi = av ? hi : 0`).
  If it were forgotten, empty ranges (len 0, `hi == lo`) would create spurious dependencies:
  a superset, so data stays the same but perf could slip. The shadow check flags it as a
  mismatch.
- **Shared `dw`:** correct only while the ISA has no op with one DRAM read plus one DRAM write.
  Add a sim assert that both valid DRAM ranges share the write role. The fallback is per-range
  bits (+1 FF/slot).
- **Unroll limits** (lesson 001624-s1): 16 slots × 13 plain `<` cells, well within slang's limit.
  No digit loops.

- `conf_s` has 13 cells: 4 DRAM (gated by `n.dw|e.dw`, these set `any` and `dram`), 8 TMEM (t×t, t×e.t2, n.t2×e.t, gated by write bits), and 1 ACT on 8/17 bits. Only its type changes for `ndep`/`ndepd`/`sfp`/`c_fp`. Nothing else is touched.
- Sim-only (`ifndef SYNTHESIS`): shadow `c_ref`/`sfp_ref[WIN]` in `fp_t` form. Every cycle with `c_v`, `$fatal` unless `conf_s(c_fp, sfp[i]) == {conflict, conflict_dram}(c_ref, sfp_ref[i])` for every valid slot. At Q→C there are also asserts that valid ACT ranges have `lo[31:8] == 0` and `hi[31:17] == 0`, and that no instruction has both a DRAM read and a DRAM write (the shared `dw` bit).
- Verified: lint is clean. test_mlp_rtl[1,2], scoreboard_stress (single slice 0 and 5, two slices 0), fuzz_single_slice[3] and attention_decode[1-8-2-100] pass. To check that the shadow check is live, I broke the ACT cell on purpose (`||` → `&&`): test_mlp_rtl[1] then hit the `$fatal` right away. The change is reverted.
- For the reviewer: the shadow check calls `conflict()` 16×/cycle in simulation, so sim is a bit slower. Synthesis logic is unaffected.
lesson: Porting the space-segregated scoreboard to the current champion worked: storing ranges by DRAM/TMEM/ACT with no space compares and hi=0 for invalid ranges (no valid bits) gave -8.8% area at 125 MHz.

title: Q-stage footprint rebalance: pre-add the product-free part of every range at S, carry-free `len != 0` at Q
